welcome.title: Clear Food, Harvest & Market Information for Rwanda
welcome.intro: AgrIntel connects weather, soil, harvest records, and daily market prices across Rwanda. We help farmers, traders, families, and agricultural leaders make timely, smart decisions.
welcome.disclaimer: Outlooks are estimates that support decisions. They are not guarantees or policy advice.

welcomeHub.title: Clear Food, Harvest & Market Information for Everyone
welcomeHub.intro: AgrIntel brings together trusted harvest records, daily market prices, and rainfall updates to make food security simple, transparent, and actionable.

whatWeDo.title: What We Do
whatWeDo.desc: We gather official farm harvest records, daily town market prices, and weather updates across all 30 districts so nobody has to guess.

whatValueWeBring.title: What Value We Bring
whatValueWeBring.desc: We protect farmers from selling at a loss, help truck drivers find profitable markets, guide families to affordable healthy food, and help leaders spot harvest shortages early.

whatToDo.title: What To Do
whatToDo.subtitle: Choose your role below to find the exact guide and tools built for you:

farmer.action: Check when to sell or store your harvest, listen to audio advice in Kinyarwanda, and see local market prices.

retailer.action: Calculate truck fuel costs, avoid food spoilage, and find which towns offer the highest profit for your harvest.

national.title: National food-security outlook
national.intro: District market-price signals for each crop, with the source, date and evidence behind every signal. Districts without approved data show as unavailable rather than being guessed.
national.scopeNote: This is a market-price signal only. Weather, soil and production signals are not yet connected, so they are not shown.
national.tableCaption: Districts and their current market signal
national.ruleTitle: How the market signal is calculated
national.ruleText: The average price of the last 3 observed months is compared with the 3 observed months before. A rise of 10% or more is moderate; a rise of 20% or more is high. Any other change is low. The rule looks at the last 9 calendar months. A district needs at least 6 observed months in that window, and its latest price must be no more than 4 months old. Older data never produces a signal.

evidence.title: District evidence
evidence.select: Choose a district in the table to see the evidence behind its signal.
evidence.noSignal: No market signal for this district and crop yet. There is not enough approved price history.
evidence.riseText: The average price over the last 3 months is {percent} above the 3 months before.
evidence.fallText: The average price over the last 3 months is {percent} below the 3 months before.
evidence.flatText: The average price over the last 3 months is about the same as the 3 months before.
evidence.uncertainty: This signal describes market prices only. It is not a forecast of production or a guarantee of future prices.
evidence.responseNote: No response is suggested automatically. Any response needs review by an expert before it is shared.

agronomic.title: District Harvest & Farming Summary
agronomic.leakageAdvice: The harvest in this district was lower than expected even though many farmers bought seeds and fertilizers. To protect your crop, always check for official Rwanda Agriculture Board (RAB) tags on seed bags and avoid buying from unsealed packets.
agronomic.climateAdvice: Crops in this area suffered from low rainfall. Where possible, water your fields using valley and marshland canals, spread dry grass or mulch over soil to keep moisture in, and plant crops with different harvest times.
agronomic.intensificationAdvice: Farmers here achieved high harvests by combining good seeds, correct fertilizer amounts, and hillside terraces. Remember to dry your harvest well before storage so it does not spoil.
agronomic.nominalAdvice: Harvests and fertilizer use in this district are normal and on target. Continue standard good farming practices and sell through your cooperative for the best price.
agronomic.noData: Official harvest baseline is not recorded for this specific crop and district combination.
agronomic.samplingWeightsNote: Based on official agricultural survey covering all districts in Rwanda

arbitrage.title: Truck Transport Cost & Profit Calculator
arbitrage.intro: Calculates profit when buying from farmers and selling at town markets, subtracting fuel expenses and food spoilage along the road.
arbitrage.sliderHelp: See how your transport profits change if pump prices rise or fall:

columns.breakeven: Highest Fuel Price You Can Afford

howToRead.title: How Transport Profits Are Calculated
howToRead.body: We calculate round-trip truck fuel costs based on distance and truck size, plus handling. We also deduct natural food spoilage (for example, fragile tomatoes lose about 8% over 100km, while potatoes lose only 1.5%). When profit is over 40 Rwf per kg, shipping to the city is worthwhile. If profit is under 10 Rwf per kg, it is better to sell locally or store your crop.

mathSection.title: Practical Calculations Behind the Guide
mathSection.subtitle: Every calculation follows clear, transparent arithmetic based on real farm harvest records, daily market prices, and truck fuel costs:

forecast.title: Price outlook
forecast.outputValue: Monthly national average price with a range
forecast.horizonValue: Up to 6 months ahead, only from the last approved month
forecast.intervalValue: About 80%, from the method's own errors on past data
forecast.note: A baseline, not a claim of predictive skill. Accuracy is reported only from real backtests below.

risk.title: District market signal
risk.note: Covers market prices only. Weather, soil and production signals are not yet connected.

auditMethod.title: Official Harvest vs. Seed & Weather Expectation Check
auditMethod.model: Expected Harvest Formula: Combining Good Seeds, Fertilizer & Rain
auditMethod.formula: Expected Harvest = Normal Yield x Weather Factor (Rain & Temperature) x Seed & Fertilizer Factor
auditMethod.residual: Harvest Difference = Actual Harvest minus Expected Target
auditMethod.leakage: Seed / Fertilizer Quality Notice: Low harvest despite good rains and heavy fertilizer use (check for counterfeit seeds or delayed deliveries)
auditMethod.climate: Drought or Rain Deficit: Low harvest caused by low rainfall or long dry spells
auditMethod.intensification: Great Harvest: District produced much more than expected thanks to good seeds, terraces, and water management
auditMethod.sampling: Calculated using official national farming survey records covering every district in Rwanda.

arbitrageMethod.title: Truck Fuel & Food Transport Profit Calculator
arbitrageMethod.formula: Take-Home Profit per Kilo = City Market Price (minus Fresh Food Spoilage) minus Farm Price minus (Truck Fuel Cost + Road Taxes + Handling)
arbitrageMethod.burnRate: Standard medium cargo truck: Uses 32 liters of diesel for every 100 km carrying up to 5,000 kg of food
arbitrageMethod.shrinkage: Food that spoils or bruises on bumpy roads: Tomatoes lose 8.0%, Irish potatoes lose 1.5%, Dry maize loses 0.5%
arbitrageMethod.fuelPolicy: Rwanda regulated diesel price: 2,927 Rwf/liter. Without government fuel support, diesel would cost 3,600 Rwf/liter, saving truckers 673 Rwf on every liter.
arbitrageMethod.breakeven: Highest Fuel Cost Before Loss: The maximum diesel price a trucker can pay before the trip stops making money.

methodology.accuracyNote: Errors come from re-running the method on past months, using only data available at each point. Lower is better. No accuracy figure is shown unless a backtest produced it.
methodology.noEvaluations: No backtest results are recorded yet. Run the forecast pipeline to produce them.
limits: Data comes from official national farming surveys, local market price checkers, farm receipts, and Rwanda Meteo weather stations.
The price outlook is a national average across markets; local prices in your village may differ.
Harvest checks and truck routes provide helpful guidelines; always confirm with your local agronomist or market cooperative before making big investments.
Price forecasts reflect typical patterns from past years and are not guarantees of future prices.
General farming tips are provided for guidance; consult a licensed agronomist or veterinary doctor for specific chemical doses or treatments.
Everything is fully available in both easy-to-read English and natural Kinyarwanda.
